active.content: FORGE CONSUMER AND DELIVERY BOUNDARY (Derek, 2026-09-03; supersedes constraint #5): Derek is the product consumer, working primarily through agents that use Forge over MCP. Agent-first does not mean metadata-only, headless-only, or no UI: OODS Foundry and Forge must produce runnable, human-inspectable greenfield artifacts and may also map into brownfield systems. No external project, consumer-pull proof, hosted endpoint, live production dependency, or Synthesis Workbench use is assumed. Hosting and headless or design-surface integrations are permitted only by an explicit later decision; public publication, paid or metered writes, and external production wiring likewise require explicit approval. Capabilities ship for Derek/agent use first. A design-surface adapter is a later evaluated option, not a currently ratified product surface. Validation may be advisory for exploratory work; the declared build or release profile is enforced for production artifacts.

archivedHistoricalConstraint5.content: CONSUMER MODEL (Derek, 2026-06-18 — standing constraint, supersedes the s115 "consumer pull" framing): Forge's consumer is AGENTS using the Forge tools via MCP. That is who we build for. (1) There is NO external project that PULLs from Forge — do NOT frame any sprint, mission, or value case around "proving a consumer pull" or any other team adopting a Forge output. (2) Forge is NOT a hosted/SaaS service and there are NO current plans to be one; nothing should assume a deployed/reachable Forge endpoint. (3) There are NO plans to use Synthesis-Workbench with the viz/export work — do not assume a Workbench surface. (4) Headless integrations are welcome IN PRINCIPLE but are a SEPARATE initiative that must be discussed explicitly BEFORE any work — as must ANY dependency that would be created for a live production site. Capabilities ship for agent use first; cross-app/production wiring is its own decision, never an implied sprint goal. This is why s115's m06 (a cmos-dashboard cutover) was correctly dropped and why the "demand signal / pull" thesis behind it is retracted.

conclusion: Constraint #7 explicitly supersedes #5. The packet must distinguish the historical #5 wording from the currently active #7 boundary; no constraint has been amended.
